title: Is it alright if I watch La Notte and then the other movies in the alienation trilogy by Antonioni?

commenti.body:
Doesn’t make a big difference. All parts of the trilogy are loose and can be watched independently. The term “trilogy” signifies a stylistic and historiographical correlation between the three films rather than a narrative one (all being produced with Monica Vitti being the muse, following the same themes and direction style).

Usually I am an advocate of watching movies chronologically so that you can see the evolution of a director’s method, but since the three films are produced within three consecutive years, you wouldn’t remark a big evolution either. So, start with whichever one you like, and enjoy :)

Yeah you can. Honestly you should probably start with La Notte, as it's the most accessible.

I'd watch L'Avventura next, even though it's probably the most challenging one. I believe L'Eclisse works the best once you've seen the first two.

As the other poster said the three films are only thematically/stylistically linked.  But, I suggest watching L'Avventura first.  It's the film that put Antonioni on the world stage.  It was also met with considerable controversy during its premiere at Cannes.  The audience booed and laughed it and many walked out.  But, the next day fellow filmmakers rallied around it and it ended up winning the Jury Prize.  It even prompted Antonioni to make a statement: [https://www.criterion.com/current/posts/100-lavventura-cannes-statement](https://www.criterion.com/current/posts/100-lavventura-cannes-statement).

L'Avventura pretty much established the cinematic language that he would then continue to explore in his later films.  There is also a pattern of the modern world encroaching on the characters that builds with each successive film.

Damn I have a totally different perspective. I found L’Avventura to be a pretty breezy watch since it’s the most plot heavy of the three. La Notte was tough for the first half but picks up in the second. And I found L’Eclisse generally difficult to sit through.
To me, L’A starts plot-heavy and compelling, but becomes very deconstructive and difficult by the end. LN is the most straightforward with its characters and situation. And L’E is totally abstract.

Watch in any order you like. I wouldn't even call them a trilogy. There isn't anything that connects those three films that wouldn't also apply to some other Antonioni films like *Il grido* or *Il deserto rosso*. People just like to lump things in groups of three for some reason.

L'avventura is the best one, but it doesn't really matter what order you watch them in. La notte is kinda the worst tho. Also it has Marcello Mastroianni who ruins everything he's in. He's like the Italian John Wayne, it makes no sense that they decided to put him in movies when he just bumbles around and acts insufferable.

> La notte is kinda the worst tho. Also it has Marcello Mastroianni who ruins everything he's in.

You lost me
Come on, watch him in a performance and then watch John. Wayne. Ford makes some great films but Wayne is always the worst part of them. I can't really say Fellini makes great films but still
I'm also driving to work and I completely forgot we were talking about Antonioni. Who does in fact make some good movies

I watched at BAM in order > Il Grido, L'Avventura, La Notte and L'Eclisse and I think you should 

a) add Il Grido

b) watch them in order

there's a method he was refining over these films, probably the greatest stretch of artistic achievement among any director , ever. They're not narratively linked, but there are similarities and it's cool to watch his process unfold. I'd want to be exposed to Monica Vitti first with L'Avventura, which is his best movie. 

If you can't be f'd, then at least watch l'Eclisse last. It feels like 'the end' of that particular period.
